name: Hopkins Falls

For a few days in early summer baby short-finned eels (elvers) can be seen leaping the rocky ledges on their migration upstream
About 15 km from Warrnambool, with viewing platforms at the falls

facts.claim: Limestone stacks off Port Campbell National Park by the Great Ocean Road, up to 50 m high
Seven of the original nine stacks remain after collapses in 2005 and 2009; six are visible from the main viewpoint
Colours shift from gold in the morning to orange and red at sunset; Little Penguins may be seen returning at dusk

name: Cape Bridgewater

facts.claim: Cape Bridgewater is a locality about 21 km south-west of Portland, on the western shore of Bridgewater Bay.
It has 4 km of sandy beach and some of the highest coastal cliffs in Victoria, around the rim of an ancient volcanic crater.
Visitors come for the Petrified Forest (rock formations like tree roots), the blowhole that throws spray skyward, and a fur seal colony viewed from a lookout.
Stony Hill above the cape is the highest cliff top on the Victorian coastline, 130 m above sea level.

name: Cape Nelson

facts.claim: Cape Nelson Lighthouse, 32 m tall, was first lit on 7 July 1884 and stands at the end of a roughly 24 km round-trip scenic drive from Portland.
Cape Nelson State Park has a 5 km lighthouse walk, a Sea Cliff Nature Walk and part of the Great South West Walk; the park is known for rare soap mallee and whale watching in migration season.
Guided lighthouse tours run daily at 11:30am and include climbing the lighthouse for views from 32 m up.
The site also has Isabella's Cafe and heritage cottages for overnight stays.

access_note: Tour is the paid part; grounds and park walks are free. Parks Victoria page carries a generic 'area closed/reported issues' banner, not specific to the lighthouse.

name: Discovery Bay Coastal Park

facts.claim: A 10,460-hectare linear coastal park running about 50 km from Cape Nelson north-west to the South Australian border.
It has rugged cliffs, long beaches, mobile dune fields, wetlands and woodland.
Victoria's highest coastal cliffs and the Cape Bridgewater fur seal colony lie within it.
Campgrounds at Lake Mombeong and Swan Lake sit near vast sand dunes; part of the Great South West Walk runs along it.

access_note: Page header shows generic 'additional visitor advice / reported issues / closed' banner labels; check Parks Victoria for current closures. Vehicle access limited to a few points.

name: Great South West Walk

facts.claim: A 262 km circular walking trail in south-west Victoria that starts and ends in Portland, established in 1981.
It crosses four environments, passing coastline, native forest in Cobboboonee and Lower Glenelg National Parks, and Discovery Bay.
It has 14 campsites that must be booked, and can be done in shorter day or overnight sections.
Volunteers from Friends of the GSWW maintain the track under Parks Victoria.

access_note: Cut Out Camp and Ralph's Bridge (Cobboboonee) closed 5 Oct 2026 until Feb 2027 for repairs. Walking the track is free; campsite fees not checked (campsites bookable, registered hikers only).

name: Port Fairy

facts.claim: A coastal town on the Moyne River about 293 km west of Melbourne, named for the sealing cutter The Fairy in 1828.
Whalers and sealers used the coast from the 1830s; John Griffiths set up a whaling station in 1835.
Tourism and fishing are its main industries, and it is home port to one of Victoria's largest fishing fleets.
Griffiths Island, joined to the town by a causeway, has a shearwater colony and a lighthouse.

name: Griffiths Island Lighthouse

facts.claim: The Port Fairy lighthouse was built of local bluestone around 1859, still guides ships into Port Fairy and sits at the island's eastern tip.
The island, about 1.5 km long, is a sanctuary reached over a causeway from town and listed on the Victorian Heritage Register.
It hosts a breeding colony of short-tailed shearwaters (muttonbirds) from September to April.
The grounds are open year round but the tower is not open to the public.

name: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape

facts.claim: UNESCO World Heritage listed (2019) cultural landscape of the Gunditjmara people, showing how they built an aquaculture system of channels and weirs over thousands of years.
Comprises three components: Budj Bim (northern, including Budj Bim National Park and Lake Condah Mission), Kurtonitj (central) and Tyrendarra (southern).
Visitors can take Gunditjmara-guided cultural tours and visit the Tae Rak Aquaculture Centre and cafe at Lake Condah.
Considered one of Victoria's earliest and largest Indigenous aquaculture ventures, with evidence of eel farming and smoking for food and trade.

access_note: Price is the Tae Rak guided cultural tour (from $89 adult); half- and full-day tours cost more. Components within the national park are free to enter. Overlaps with mount-eccles-national-park (Budj Bim National Park): consider whether both stay.

name: Mount Eccles National Park

facts.claim: Now officially named Budj Bim National Park (Budj Bim formerly Mount Eccles), co-managed by Parks Victoria and Gunditj Mirring Traditional Owners.
Has a tranquil crater lake, lava canals and caves in a bushland setting, with four walking options including the crater rim and lava flow canals.
Manna Gums in the campground are a favourite food of koalas.
Budj Bim is a volcano rising to 178 m in south-west Victoria; the easiest route up is the Lava Canal track.
